sections.title: A pale-leaved Texas yucca
sections.text: Yucca pallida is a perennial native to central Texas. It forms a low rosette of glaucous blue-grey leaves, generally 18–35 cm long and 2–4 cm wide. The illustrated flowering stalk can bring the whole plant to about 1.3–2.5 m; its pale flowers and dry, three-chambered capsule are consistent with botanical descriptions.

sections.title: Flowering and food
sections.text: The species bears branched panicles of flowers with pale greenish centres and white margins, followed by a dry capsule containing seeds. Reliable species-specific food guidance was not found in the cited sources; unlike some other yuccas, no edible use is asserted here.
